_readme: Source data for the 10 comparison pages. Edit here, then run `npm run build:comparisons` (rewrites the page bodies in content/pages). Competitor facts must come only from the competitor's own public pages; record the URL and the date you checked it. Re-check at least every 6 months, sooner when a company changes its pricing.

ypn.summary: YPN USA is a mortgage growth platform for licensed loan officers: Cerebro, an AI growth assistant; local pages, borrower funnels and Google Business Profile support under your own brand; automated follow-up; Realtor co-marketing tools; and a ZIP that is not assigned to another loan officer on the platform while your paid plan is active.
ypn.pricing: Free $0 (no credit card, no ZIP). Pro $99/mo and Growth $199/mo each include a protected ZIP. Exclusive $299/mo adds ZIP code lockout exclusivity. Paid plans include a 15-day free trial and can be cancelled online anytime.
ypn.isNot: YPN USA is not a lender, not a lead vendor that resells the same contacts, and not a replacement for your CRM or loan origination system. It does not guarantee leads, rankings, referrals or closings.

workflowStages.desc: Staying in front of past borrowers for refinance, purchase and referrals.

competitors.workflowNote: Bonzo is strongest once a lead exists. YPN USA is strongest before that: creating the inquiry and making the first response. Many loan officers would use a CRM like Bonzo next to YPN USA, not instead of it.
competitors.verdict: Choose Bonzo if your problem is follow-up volume and you already have the leads. Choose YPN USA if your problem is not having enough new local conversations. If you have both problems, YPN USA's Pro plan plus your existing CRM is the lower-cost starting point to test.

faq.q: Is YPN USA a Bonzo alternative?
faq.a: Only partly. Bonzo is an outreach and nurture CRM for contacts you already have. YPN USA focuses on creating new local demand and the first response, with automated follow-up included. They overlap on follow-up but solve different main problems.

faq.q: Does Bonzo provide mortgage leads?
faq.a: Bonzo's site does not describe selling or generating leads. It describes capturing, uploading and following up with leads from your own sources, plus a MonitorBase add-on for past-client signals.

faq.q: How much does Bonzo cost compared with YPN USA?
faq.a: Bonzo lists its Solo plan at $150 per seat per month; team and enterprise pricing are not published. YPN USA has a free plan, and paid plans at $99, $199 and $299 per month. Prices checked on each company's site on November 5, 2026.

faq.q: Can I use YPN USA and Bonzo together?
faq.a: Yes. YPN USA is not a CRM replacement. A common setup is YPN USA for local visibility and first response, and a CRM like Bonzo for long-term pipeline management.

faq.q: Which is better for a solo loan officer?
faq.a: If you have plenty of leads but slow follow-up, Bonzo. If you need more new conversations in your own market, YPN USA, starting on the free plan.

competitors.workflowNote: Homebot works at the back end of the loan lifecycle (past clients and prospects you already have). YPN USA works at the front end (new local borrowers). They rarely compete; most loan officers who need both would run them side by side.
competitors.verdict: If your past-client database is your best asset, Homebot is the better fit. If you need borrowers who aren't in your database yet, YPN USA is. They complement each other more than they compete.

faq.q: Is Homebot a lead generation tool?
faq.a: Homebot describes itself as a homeowner engagement platform and mentions AI-driven lead generation, but its examples focus on clients and prospects you add, such as re-engaging past borrowers. It is strongest for retention and repeat business.

faq.q: How much does Homebot cost for loan officers?
faq.a: Homebot lists Starter at $125/mo, Pro at $225/mo and Unlimited at $300/mo, each with a one-time $100 setup fee, on its pricing page checked November 5, 2026. YPN USA has a free plan and paid plans at $99, $199 and $299 per month.

faq.q: Can I use YPN USA and Homebot together?
faq.a: Yes. YPN USA brings in new local borrowers; Homebot keeps them engaged after closing. The tools cover different stages.

faq.q: Which is better for a newer loan officer?
faq.a: A newer loan officer usually has a small past-client list, which limits what Homebot can do. YPN USA focuses on building new demand, so it is usually the better first tool.

faq.q: Does YPN USA send equity reports?
faq.a: No. Equity and home value reports are Homebot's core product, not YPN USA's.

competitors.name: LendingTree

prosThem: Large, established national consumer brand
Volume is available quickly
Targeting options and a lender portal for data
consThem: Pricing is not published, so cost per loan is hard to estimate up front
The borrower reviews several loan offers, so you compete at the point of contact

competitors.workflowNote: LendingTree supplies demand at the very start of the funnel and hands you the rest. YPN USA covers the start too, but by building assets you keep (pages, profile, partner relationships), plus the first response and follow-up.
competitors.verdict: LendingTree suits lenders who need volume now and have the budget and call capacity to compete for it. YPN USA suits loan officers who would rather build a local source of borrowers that keeps working without paying per inquiry. Some use both while local demand ramps up.

faq.q: Are LendingTree leads shared with other lenders?
faq.a: LendingTree's partner page doesn't say. It describes borrowers completing a qualification form and then reviewing loan offers, so expect the borrower to compare more than one lender. Ask LendingTree directly how many lenders each request goes to.

faq.q: How much do LendingTree leads cost?
faq.a: LendingTree does not publish lender pricing on its partner pages (checked November 5, 2026). YPN USA publishes its plans: Free $0, Pro $99/mo, Growth $199/mo, Exclusive $299/mo.

faq.q: Is YPN USA a lead vendor like LendingTree?
faq.a: No. YPN USA does not resell contacts. It gives you the tools to build your own local source of borrowers and respond to them, and it does not guarantee lead volume.

faq.q: Can an individual loan officer join LendingTree?
faq.a: The partner page invites lenders to "join our lender network" but doesn't list eligibility rules. Contact LendingTree for requirements.

faq.q: Which is faster: LendingTree or YPN USA?
faq.a: Marketplace leads arrive faster. Local visibility through YPN USA takes time to build, but it does not stop when you stop paying per lead.

competitors.verdict: Zillow Flex is not an option for loan officers; it's an agent program that sits next to Zillow Home Loans. If your Realtor partners rely on Flex, a direct local presence through YPN USA is a way to keep your own pipeline.

faq.q: Can mortgage loan officers join Zillow Flex?
faq.a: Zillow's Flex page describes the program for agents, brokers and teams. Loan officers are not listed as eligible (checked November 5, 2026).

faq.q: How does Zillow Flex work?

faq.q: Do Zillow Flex agents have to use Zillow Home Loans?
faq.a: Zillow's Flex page promotes Zillow Home Loans as a lending partner for agents' clients. It doesn't say agents are required to use it.

faq.q: How can a loan officer compete with Zillow Home Loans?
faq.a: Be visible to borrowers before they reach a portal, respond fast, and give Realtor partners a co-marketing reason to work with you. Those are the parts YPN USA is built for.

competitors.description: YPN USA vs BNTouch mortgage CRM: features, published pricing, pros, cons and where each fits in a loan officer's workflow. Sourced and dated.
competitors.category: Mortgage CRM, texting and database mining
competitors.whatItIs: BNTouch is a mortgage CRM "built only for mortgage since 2004," with texting automation, campaigns, two-way LOS sync, opportunity mining on your database and an optional managed "White Glove" service.
competitors.pricing: BNTouch CRM: $95 per user per month for 2 to 10 users, or $165 per month for a single user. Custom pricing for 10+ users (12-month contract). New Loan Opportunity Mining and White Glove: priced on a call. No free trial.

features.ypn: Create new local demand and respond to it
features.them: Run your pipeline: CRM, texting, campaigns, LOS sync

features.label: Lead sources
features.ypn: Your own local pages, profile, content and Realtor partners
features.them: Integrates 100+ lead providers (e.g. Zillow, LendingTree) plus mining your own database

features.label: Campaigns and texting
features.ypn: Automated follow-up
features.them: 400+ pre-built mortgage campaigns and texting automation

features.label: LOS integration
features.ypn: Not a CRM or LOS replacement
features.them: Two-way sync with Encompass, Calyx, BytePro, MeridianLink, LendingPad

features.label: Websites
features.ypn: Local pages, borrower funnels, Google Business Profile support
features.them: Mortgage websites plus SEO

features.label: AI
features.ypn: Cerebro AI growth assistant
features.them: MAIA mortgage AI (included)

features.label: Territory
features.ypn: One protected ZIP per paid plan; ZIP lockout on Exclusive
features.them: None

features.label: Published starting price
features.ypn: $0 Free; paid from $99/mo with a 15-day trial
features.them: $165/mo single user; $95/user/mo for 2 to 10; no free trial

competitors.fitsThem: Loan officers and mortgage teams who want a full mortgage CRM with LOS sync, campaigns and database mining, and are ready to commit without a trial.
competitors.fitsYpn: Loan officers who want new local borrowers under their own brand and a lighter, lower-cost starting point.
prosThem: Mortgage-only CRM with a long track record
Two-way LOS sync with major systems
Large library of pre-built campaigns
Database mining for credit and equity signals (extra fee)
consThem: No free trial
Key add-ons priced on a call
Contract required for larger teams
prosYpn: Free plan and 15-day trials
Focus on new local demand under your name
Protected ZIP on every paid plan
consYpn: Not a full CRM; no LOS sync described
Fewer pre-built campaigns
Local results take time and are not guaranteed
competitors.workflowNote: BNTouch is a system of record for your pipeline and past clients. YPN USA is a source of new local demand. Teams that need both often keep their CRM and add YPN USA for local visibility.
competitors.verdict: Pick BNTouch if you need a mortgage CRM with LOS sync and are ready to commit. Pick YPN USA if your gap is new local borrowers and you want to start free. They can work together.

faq.q: How much does BNTouch cost?
faq.a: BNTouch lists $165 per month for a single user and $95 per user per month for 2 to 10 users, with custom pricing above 10 users; Opportunity Mining and White Glove are priced on a call (checked November 5, 2026). YPN USA has a free plan and paid plans at $99, $199 and $299 per month.

faq.q: Does BNTouch have a free trial?
faq.a: Its pricing page says no. YPN USA's paid plans include a 15-day free trial, and the Free plan needs no credit card.

faq.q: Is YPN USA a CRM?
faq.a: No. YPN USA focuses on local visibility, lead capture and follow-up. It is not a replacement for a mortgage CRM or LOS.

faq.q: Does BNTouch generate leads?
faq.a: BNTouch integrates with 100+ lead providers and mines your existing database for opportunities. Its site does not say it sells leads itself.

faq.q: Can I use YPN USA with BNTouch?
faq.a: Yes. Many loan officers keep their CRM and add YPN USA for local demand.

competitors.workflowNote: Both use AI, at different stages. LoanOfficer.ai maximizes what you get from inquiries and past clients you already have. YPN USA focuses on generating new local inquiries. The overlap is the first response.
competitors.verdict: If you have the inquiries and the database, LoanOfficer.ai squeezes more out of them. If you need more new inquiries in your market, start with YPN USA.

faq.q: How much does LoanOfficer.ai cost?
faq.a: LoanOfficer.ai lists Starter at $197/mo for 2 seats, Team at $397/mo and Brokerage at $697/mo, with a one-time $299 setup fee and $1 for the first 14 days (checked November 5, 2026). YPN USA has a free plan and paid plans at $99, $199 and $299 per month.

faq.q: Does LoanOfficer.ai generate leads?
faq.a: Its site describes answering inquiries, booking appointments and reactivating your database, with lead-provider integrations. It doesn't describe selling or generating new leads itself.

faq.q: Which has better AI follow-up?
faq.a: LoanOfficer.ai's AI follow-up and appointment booking are its core product. YPN USA includes AI follow-up as part of a broader local growth system. If response automation is your main need, LoanOfficer.ai goes deeper.

faq.q: Can I use both?
faq.a: Yes. YPN USA can bring in new local inquiries, and a CRM like LoanOfficer.ai can work them and your past clients.

faq.q: Is Real Geeks good for loan officers?
faq.a: Real Geeks is built for real estate agents, teams and brokers. Its site does not describe features for mortgage lenders or loan officers (checked November 5, 2026).

faq.q: How much does Real Geeks cost?

faq.q: Does Real Geeks provide leads?
faq.a: Yes, through paid-ad lead packages for buyers and sellers, which are aimed at agents.

faq.q: What is a Real Geeks alternative for mortgage?
faq.a: Look for a tool built for loan officers. YPN USA focuses on local mortgage visibility, follow-up and Realtor co-marketing for loan officers.
